source.range_scope: Physical terminal elimination, positive task effects, paired acquisition and calibration-mixture limitation.

source_excerpts.text:
5. Positive finite task representation from the physical readout boundary
========================================================================
Let a raw macro before its final Pauli repair output logical system L,
ancillas A=A1...Am and memory M. The state/channel before these final reads
can be arbitrary. For a QND readout word w on the ancillas,
  K_w=sum_mu k_w(mu) Pi_mu,
where mu in {0,1}^m labels their joint Pauli eigenprojectors. After actual trace,
  Tr_A[K_w rho K_w*]
    =sum_mu |k_w(mu)|^2 Tr_A[Pi_mu rho Pi_mu].             (1)
Cross terms disappear because distinct local eigenprojectors have disjoint
support in the subsystem being traced. This identity includes arbitrary
logical-reference-memory correlations. It is not a claim that mu was measured
or supplied to the observer before the weak sequence.

Actual matched outer Pauli frames at the logical input/output, with keys
retired, reduce each virtual mu branch to Kraus operators
  s_L tensor K_(s,mu,l),       s in {I,X,Y,Z}.
Define
  F_(s,mu)=sum_l K_(s,mu,l)* K_(s,mu,l) >=0,
  sum_(s,mu) F_(s,mu)=I_M.
These effects need not commute. At the actual pre-use memory marginal rho_M,
  W_(s,mu)=Tr[F_(s,mu) rho_M].                            (2)
The acquired-record law is
  p(s,w)=sum_mu W_(s,mu) L(w|mu),
  L(w|mu)=|k_w(mu)|^2.                                  (3)

The unknown native dynamics appears in a positive task vector W with
D=4*2^m entries. The known, physically implemented observation appears in L.
For k logical qubits the same argument gives 4^k*2^m entries, not a polynomial
bound in arbitrary boundary size. For a nonidentity Clifford target, label
errors in that target frame; a classical tableau does not physically implement
the target.

For fixed eta and L identical QND probes, the full word likelihood depends
only on the count k_i of its negative marks:
  L(w|mu)=product_i [(1+eta)/2]^[mu_i k_i+(1-mu_i)(L-k_i)]
                    [(1-eta)/2]^[(1-mu_i)k_i+mu_i(L-k_i)].
Therefore the complete fine word has an exact count statistic in this physical
setting. The code retains all words until that reduction; it does not assume
that coarse majority signs contain the same predictive information.

For eta=3/5, exact likelihood comparisons reduce to powers of4 and positive
integer additions. The implementation uses integer ratios, avoiding an
uncontrolled floating-point underflow or precision p

source.quote: 2. Remaining value of perfect syndrome information
source.range_scope: Perfect-syndrome value, greedy parity obstruction, model-average capped regret and paid finite schedule.

source_excerpts.text:
2. Remaining value of perfect syndrome information
==================================================
On a received branch v let
  U_(s,mu)=What_(s,mu) L(v|mu), T=sum_(s,mu) U_(s,mu),
  C=max_s sum_mu U_(s,mu), P=sum_mu max_s U_(s,mu).
The current modeled success probability is C/T. If the observer were given
the exact mu for free, the best success would be P/T. This unavailable perfect
readout is only a mathematical upper benchmark. Define
  G(v)=(P-C)/T.                                           (2)
Convexity of max gives G>=0. Any further syndrome-only experiment is a
stochastic kernel acting on mu. Its optimal mean success cannot exceed P/T:
after learning mu, one could reproduce that additional experiment and use its
same final action. Thus no admissible continuation of terminal readout can
improve modeled success by more than G(v).

This bound concerns the chosen terminal interface. It does not prove that
all physics lacks information about the error or rule out a different
interaction, a new sensor, or an acquired coherent control operation.

The controller stops when G<=epsilon and applies the Pauli attaining C.
The test is an exact integer inequality, so it does not infer smallness from
floating underflow or assume a probability margin that was not acquired.
It may stop with a substantial total logical error when no remaining
syndrome information can resolve that error.

3. Avoiding a decisive greedy-information failure
=================================================
Pure one-step information greed can stop too early. Let two hidden syndrome
bits be independent uniform bits, and let the logical error be X exactly when
their parity is 1. Learning either bit alone leaves parity uniform, so the
expected one-step task improvement is EXACTLY ZERO. At eta=3/5, after one weak
probe of each bit, the Bayes success is 17/25, a gain 9/50=.18 over 1/2. A rule
that refuses every locally zero-value probe never discovers the joint benefit.

The implemented construction therefore uses a fair schedule: one complete
round contains one actual probe on every one of the six readout lanes. It
rechecks (2) after each round and stops after at most 35 rounds. No claim of
globally optimal sensor allocation is made. The fair schedule prevents the
one-step-value trap, while the remaining-perfect-information bound supplies
a meaningful stopping criterion. Bounded lookahead o

9. Fresh verification of the entire delivered operation
======================================================
The whole raw encode/transmit/read/recover macro is now the native channel
tested by the predecessor's secret-slot theorem. All internal preparation,
gating, link, readout and decoder faults lie inside that operation. There is
one outer validation packet, not a product of inner gate acceptances.

For packet length n, put the unprobed unknown payload at a uniformly private
slot J, audit every other slot with fresh settings, run all slots, and accept
only if all audits pass. Endpoint buffers are isolated and roles/axes are
hidden from the macro. Frame keys are retired. Internal fine records can be
retained. The policy is frozen for the packet.

For a one-qubit identity target let
  a=(1+gamma)/2,
  b=(1-gamma/3)/2,
  beta_n=max_(1<=h<=n) (h/n) a^(n-h) b^(h-1).             (11)
The accepted bad CP map has effect <=beta_n I. There exists an ideal
identity-on-data operation with the SAME accepted environment/record filter
such that its half-diamond distance from the real accepted map is <=beta_n.
The bound includes arbitrary untouched references and continuing quantum M.

For n64 and L35 outer probes, b/a<=1/2, and
  beta_64=a^63/64=.01555775822794474 <1/64.
This is an accepted ERROR WEIGHT. It is not an error probability conditioned
on acceptance equal to1/64. If payload/reference starts independently of the
apparatus, a normalized accepted-channel allowance divides by its actual
acceptance probability. With preexisting correlations, compare to the same
ideal environment filter, which may itself steer the data/reference marginal.
The theorem does not give a uniform certainty statement for each fine record.

Every packet has a formal positive floor b^(n-1), but this can be exponentially
small and is not an economical success guarantee. A rejected unknown input is
consumed; it cannot simply be retried as if it were a newly prepared ancilla.
Buffer faults, role/axis leakage and deviations of trusted full instruments
must be separately charged. They are not acquired by observing native success.
